and failure, and so also with new cheerfulness and kindness.
We are best able to face our life of work and our weekly
tasks when, with all our industry and conscientiousness, we
have gained an inner detachment from them, when we know
that our work is not the ultimate value and does not exhaust
the potentialities of our being. Work is not our master.
God is our Master!
III
"Take my yoke upon you and learn from me." If the
promise "I will refresh you" is to be valid for us, then of
course we must submit ourselves to the law of Christ and take
upon us His yoke. He says to us: "My yoke is easy and my
burden is light." But only he experiences this who really
takes upon him the yoke of Christ. For the truth is that those
who do not at all feel themselves to be weary and heavy
laden, recoil from taking the yoke of Christ and look upon
it as harsh and crushing. The real meaning and blessing of
Sunday is concealed from such people. They too celebrate
Sunday but they misunderstand and abuse it.
We are of course aware that there are many people for
whom the work in which they are engaged during the week
does not constitute the meaning of their lives. They are not
absorbed in their work. Their work remains something
external to themselves; it is not for them a fulfilment of life
but only a means of livelihood; and no doubt they feel their
work to be a burden. For the real essence of life is for them
the excitement of pleasure. There is no need to dwell on this
misuse of Sunday which makes of Sunday not the Lord's
Day, not a time of quiet and worship, but a time of noisy
activity; not rest but sheer pleasure-seeking, not a time for
self-recollection but a time for escaping from oneselt, not
an opportunity for inner concentration of being, but an
opportunity for distraction and amusement. Such people not
only miss the real spiritual blessing of Sunday but also for the
most part the gift which it brings of outward quiet; and
Monday morning finds them prostrated and peevish.
